ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against at least the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Cyprus MOKAS/FIU records. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval under Law 188(I)/2007 and FATF Recommendation 12. Screening must be refreshed periodically and before each new business relationship or LC transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) e-Filing portal and Company Name Approval System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be submitted in Latin characters using an English transliteration and must include the suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Greek-language names are accepted where romanized. Any proposed non-Latin-script name requires a certified transliteration into the Latin alphabet. The name must not be misleading, identical, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: HOLDING or GROUP where they imply an unlicensed financial group
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Cyprus name reservations are valid for six months and may not be extended; a new application must be resubmitted if incorporation is not completed before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with DRCOR within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching a legal opinion and, where applicable, the consent of the relevant supervisory authority. Further review may be sought from the Minister of Energy, Commerce and Industry, with final recourse to the Administrative Court of the Republic of Cyprus under Article 146 of the Constitution. For names containing a sensitive token, the relevant ministerial or sectoral clearance must be obtained before re-submission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered virtual office is permissible and DRCOR will accept a Cyprus service-provider address; however, for a bitumen wholesale trading company relying on letter-of-credit settlement, banks and AML obliged entities will require demonstrable commercial substance in Cyprus, including local management availability, records custody, and a physical or serviced office where directors and UBOs can be met. A pure brass-plate arrangement is not recommended and may elevate tax and AML risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% - low-to-moderate risk of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first operating year, increasing to more than 25% if the entity operates from a shared residential address, fails to respond to AML queries, or undertakes high-risk counterparty transactions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113, as amended; sections 3–5 (formation and registration), 12 (registered office), 20 (appointment of directors) and the Companies Law (Fees) Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 (Application for Registration of a Company) accompanied by the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. A Cyprus private limited company may incorporate with one ordinary share of EUR 1.00. No escrow account, bank deposit certificate, or capital release permission is required. The issued and paid-up capital must be truthfully stated in the annual return filed with the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CYPRUS LIMITED

The sole subscriber and the appointed director, having subscribed to the Memorandum and Articles of Association, hereby unanimously resolve:

1. The initial share capital of EUR 1.00, represented by one ordinary share, is subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholder.
2. The registered office of the company is adopted at [postal address], Nicosia, Cyprus for statutory service of process.
3. [Name] is appointed first director; [Name] is appointed company secretary.
4. The director is authorised to open bank accounts, engage an independent tax advisor, and file all registrations required by Cypriot law.

Approved on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and UBO Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (CAPANET electronic company registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form HE2 for name reservation through the CAPANET portal or the Registry counter. Verify the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Cyprus company or trademark. Provide a declaration of the ultimate beneficial owner in accordance with the Cyprus Companies Law and the Beneficial Ownership Registers Law.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid passport of each subscriber
Consent letter if the name contains a regulated word such as 'Group', 'Bank' or 'Insurance'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name application with a secondary proposed name. If an objection is raised by a third party, respond within the statutory deadline and, if necessary, appeal the Registrar's decision under the procedures of the Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal adviser and notary, followed by filing with the Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English using the standard Cyprus private limited company form. The objects clause must cover wholesale supply, storage and trading of drummed and bagged bitumen and asphalt products. Each subscriber must sign the Memorandum before a witness; signatures may be notarised or apostilled if executed outside Cyprus.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of residential address of each subscriber
Written consent of proposed directors and company secretary
Declaration of compliance with Cyprus Companies Law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the constitutional documents, amend the relevant clauses and re-submit. Provide certified English or Greek translations if any document is challenged on linguistic or formal grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (CAPANET online filing window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form HE1 together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the name reservation certificate, and the statutory declaration of compliance prepared by the legal practitioner. Pay the prescribed filing fee via the portal or at the Department's treasury window. The application is then examined by the Registrar's staff.
required_dossiers: Form HE1 duly completed and signed
Statutory Declaration of Compliance by the legal practitioner or a subscribing director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registrar in writing within 14 days with corrected documents or explanations. If the application is formally rejected, correct the defects and re-lodge the application with a further fee, or apply to the District Court for review of the Registrar's decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit Extraction
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, collect the original Certificate of Incorporation online or from the Registry. Order certified copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association and register the company with the Beneficial Ownership Register. Obtain the corporate seal, share certificate book, and statutory registers from a licensed corporate service provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains typographical errors, apply in writing for correction under the Registrar's rectification procedure. If the certificate is lost, submit a statutory declaration and request a certified replacement copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Republic of Cyprus; Social Insurance Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate income tax registration form with the District Tax Office following issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. Apply for VAT registration under Form VAT 101 if taxable supply turnover will exceed the EUR 15,600 threshold or if voluntary registration is desirable for input VAT recovery. Register as an employer with Social Insurance Services and the Department of Labour Inspection if the company will have employees.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and addresses of directors, secretary, and ultimate beneficial owner
Registered office address confirmation (lease or title deed)
Bank account opening confirmation or intention letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Department requests additional UBO information, provide the certified ownership chart and passport copies. If mandatory VAT registration is not yet required, apply for voluntary registration or notify the District Tax Office of exemption status by filing a written explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Industrial / Physical Licensing (as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry; Department of Labour Inspection; Local Fire Services and Municipal Licensing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the company will operate only as a wholesale distributor or will also maintain physical storage of drummed bitumen. If only trading, no central sectoral industrial license is required. If a storage warehouse is used, obtain a municipal commercial premises permit, fire safety approval, and structural certification for the racking and storage floor. Submit an environmental registration only if the storage activity meets the thresholds for waste or hazardous-substances registration.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title for the storage premises
Structural load certificate issued by a registered civil engineer
Waste management contract (if any waste residues are generated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority issues a compliance notice, cure the specified defects within the stated deadline and submit a written response with supporting certificates. If a license is refused, request written reasons and appeal to the Ministry or the District Court, depending on the nature of the refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Republic of Cyprus
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory sectoral operating license for wholesale distribution of ISIC 4661 bitumen and asphalt products; a municipal trading/warehouse permit is required only if the company maintains physical storage premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, Republic of Cyprus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for pure wholesale trading and distribution under ISIC 4661. A light environmental registration and waste-handling notification under the Cyprus Waste Law will apply if the company stores drummed bitumen at a fixed warehouse exceeding annual waste transfer thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process emissions are generated by wholesale distribution. If a storage facility is operated, the site must have impermeable, bunded containment with 110% capacity of the largest stored container to prevent soil and groundwater contamination. Any wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must comply with Cypriot water discharge permits and waste-water limits. Bitumen waste consignments must be documented and transferred only to licensed waste managers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and civil defense clearance are required for any storage premises, including fire extinguishers, hydrants, escape routes, and emergency lighting. Structural load inspections by a registered civil engineer are required for racking systems and storage floors. Workplace occupational clearance must be obtained from the Department of Labour Inspection under the Safety and Health at Work Law (Law 89(I)-1996), including a site-specific risk assessment, first-aid provisions, and employee training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Cyprus Tax Department (Τμήμα Φορολογίας / Department of Taxation), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Cyprus. Electronic filing portal: TAXISnet (https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy). VAT registration, VAT returns and EU sales lists are lodged through the Tax Department's ARIADNE (Αριάδνη) electronic VAT platform. Customs export processing is handled by the Cyprus Customs and Excise Department (Τμήμα Τελωνείων) under the EU Export Control System (ECS/ECS2), requiring a CY-prefixed EORI number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Company registration: A Cyprus private limited company (CY_LTD) is incorporated with the Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR); Cyprus imposes no minimum capital requirement and foreign shareholding is fully permitted. Step 2 – Automatic income-tax TIN: Upon incorporation, DRCOR transmits the company profile to the Cyprus Tax Department, which automatically allocates an 8-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN); no separate income-tax application is required for a Cypriot-incorporated trading vehicle that is managed and controlled in Cyprus. Step 3 – Foreign-company TIN: A foreign entity that has a Cyprus permanent establishment or central management and control must file the income-tax company registration form (T.D. 2001 or the electronic equivalent) with the Tax Department, attaching certified constitutional documents, certificate of registration/good standing, board resolution, power of attorney, and proof of the Cyprus establishment. Step 4 – VAT registration: File Form VAT 101 (Application for VAT Registration) through the Tax Department's ARIADNE electronic VAT portal. The Cyprus VAT registration certificate bears the VAT number in the format 'CY' + 8-digit TIN + one check letter. Non-EU-established applicants must simultaneously appoint a tax representative established in Cyprus under the Cyprus VAT Law. Step 5 – Customs/EORI: Obtain a Cyprus EORI number (prefix 'CY') from Cyprus Customs to lodge electronic export declarations and transport manifests. Step 6 – Ancillary registrations: Where the company has Cypriot payroll, register with Social Insurance Services (GESY) and the employers' PAYE/health levy.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus domestic law has no check-the-box or look-through entity classification election; a Cyprus limited company is inherently opaque and taxed at entity level (12.5% corporate income tax on worldwide income for resident companies). Available statutory elections relevant to a bitumen trading group include: (i) group relief election for intra-group loss surrender; (ii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election on new qualifying equity; (iii) Intellectual Property (IP) box election (80% deemed deduction on qualifying IP income); (iv) tonnage tax election for qualifying shipping/maritime operations; (v) deemed dividend distribution election for close companies under the Special Defence Contribution regime; (vi) pooled foreign tax credit election; and (vii) merger/division roll-over elections. Hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD II (Law 141(I)/2021, in force 1 January 2022) apply mandatorily and non-electively to hybrid entities, hybrid instruments and double-deduction arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Kentriki Trapeza Kyprou), Nicosia, Cyprus
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Cyprus is a Eurozone member and the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no domestic exchange-control laws restricting the use or transfer of euros. Dividend distributions and branch profit remittances by a Cyprus-resident private limited company are generally free from statutory withholding taxes to non-resident shareholders, subject to EU anti-money-laundering, sanctions screening, and standard bank verification requirements. The Central Bank of Cyprus retains prudential and balance-of-payments statistical monitoring but does not impose conversion requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export-proceeds surrender rule exists for Cyprus exporters. Export receipts for bitumen and asphalt products sold on containerized wholesale terms may be retained in euros or in any permissible foreign currency and need not be converted. There is no fixed statutory timeline for forced repatriation; proceeds should be domiciled with a Cyprus/EU-licensed banking institution under normal commercial settlement terms and be supported by export documentation, freight documentation, and customs declarations for tax and CBC statistical reporting purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Trade-Finance Settlement Facilities
Operational Treasury and FX Hedging Account
Commercial Letter-of-Credit and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a supplemental digital rail only. Legal constraints are significant for offshore non-EEA electronic money institutions; such entities generally lack the required Cyprus/EU authorisation and cannot provide compliant SEPA or euro clearing services. An EU-licensed EMI with a valid passport into Cyprus, including a Cyprus-authorised Electronic Money Institution under the Payment Services Law and Central Bank of Cyprus supervision, may be used for ancillary low-value payments, but it must not replace the primary tier-1 Cypriot banking relationship. Offshore EMIs are not acceptable for trade settlements involving letters of credit or import/export cargo financing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Cyprus corporate KYC rules require clear identification of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. Standard practice now assumes that at least one director and the authorised signatories attend an in-person interview at a Cyprus branch, with original passports and proof of residential address. Remote opening is possible at some banks through video-identification only when accompanied by apostilled or notarised corporate documents, a credible banking referrer, and an enhanced compliance review. For a newly incorporated Cyprus Ltd with non-resident shareholders, physical attendance in Nicosia or Limassol remains the compliance-safe and operationally preferable route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, OFAC, UN/EU licensing, or adverse-media flags against suppliers, refineries, or trade corridors in the bitumen supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a live sanctions and PEP screening report for every counterparty, corporate registry extracts, refinery of origin certificates, supplier provenance declarations, end-user declarations, full shipping documentation including bills of lading, cargo manifests, customs declarations, and a board-approved trade counterparty clearance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ultimate-ownership structure, nominee shareholdings, or intervention by an offshore trust or management company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete UBO register required under the Cyprus Companies Law, an organisational chart, full shareholder ledger, trust deed or foundation documents if applicable, certified passports of all UBOs, independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports, and a signed KYC witness certificate from a qualified fiduciary or accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment patterns or trade-finance mismatches, including split payments, prepayment to jurisdictions with weak AML enforcement, or over/under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed commercial contracts, proforma invoices, commercial invoices corresponding to each transfer, independent tank/container inspection certificates, Intertek/SGS or similar quality reports, customs export declarations, insurance certificates, and an audit-trail narrative demonstrating consistency between the physical cargo, the invoice amount, and the payment date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wires received from non-EU banks or from third-country payment intermediaries not meeting Cypriot correspondent-banking standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Include a SWIFT MT103 copy for each inbound transfer, beneficiary and originator tax identification numbers, the bank confirmation of the underlying source account, the commercial contract reference, sample bill of lading or logistics waybill, and an explanation addressing the economic purpose and routing necessity of using each intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections should be executed as a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer to the Cyprus Ltd corporate account using the beneficiary IBAN and BIC. The payment message field 70 must state 'Capital Contribution – Equity Subscription' and reference the board resolution and share allotment number. On the Cypriot bank's declaration form, where requested, the payment should be categorised as a direct-investment capital transaction. The supporting verification bundle must include the board resolution authorising the capital increase, minutes of the share allotment, updated register of members, evidence of source of funds from the investor's bank, and certified KYC/CTF forms. No Central Bank of Cyprus approval or exchange-control permit is required for a lawful euro-denominated parity capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to refineries and bitumen suppliers should be cleared via standard SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for routine commercial settlements, with full invoice references and the applicable ISIC 4661 wholesale trade documentation. For high-value containerized bitumen cargoes, an irrevocable, confirmed at-sight documentary letter of credit issued in accordance with UCP 600 is the recommended clearing rail, with the SWIFT MT700 message incorporating required documents, including commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, quality certificate, and insurance policy. Letters of credit should be issued in the transaction currency, typically EUR or USD, and should be routed through a tier-1 Cyprus bank to a reputable confirming or negotiating bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards with a documented underlying import or export exposure
FX swaps used for temporary liquidity rebalancing in trade finance flows
Cross-currency interest rate swaps linked to trade-loan facilities denominated in USD or EUR
Conditional or cancellable FX forward contracts on verified future receivables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid non-euro currencies, executed through a licensed EU credit institution and strictly supported by a genuine trade transaction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of incorporation (annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default fines under Companies Law Cap.113, including daily continuing default fines on the company and its officers; repeated non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with Form HE32 within the same 42-day period following the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors liable to default fines for failing to lay audited financial statements; persistent non-filing may expose the company to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (UBO Register Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Central Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June each calendar year; within 30 days after any change, including share transfers that alter beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties under Cyprus AML/UBO legislation may include fines and imprisonment; willful non-compliance may also lead to strike-off for persistent registry failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for every Cyprus private limited company regardless of turnover, total assets, or employee count; there is no small-company audit exemption under Cyprus Companies Law Cap.113.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the European Union (EU-IFRS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any share transfer affecting beneficial ownership must be recorded in the Register of Members and the Register of Beneficial Owners and reported to the Central Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 days. Additionally, by 30 June of each year, the company must electronically confirm the continued accuracy of its UBO data through the Registrar's Beneficial Owner Submission Form.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP regime exemption (nexus approach); Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity (based on 10-year government bond yield, capped at relevant rate, applied to qualifying new equity); tonnage tax/shipping regime not applicable; membership interest and qualified dividend participation exemption under Art. 14(1)(c) for disposed securities; no payroll-based credits for commodity distribution

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form TD4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via Taxisnet (AADE? no - Cyprus Tax Department 'Taxisnet')
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 months after the end of the tax year (calendar year); e.g., FYE 31 December 2025 due 31 March 2027; payment of final tax due on filing; provisional tax in installments due 31 July, 30 September and 15 December of the tax year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per audited financial statements (accounting profit before tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full Cyprus-sourced income and foreign income attributable to the Cyprus permanent establishment (PE); for a non-resident company without a PE, no TD4 is due

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowed expenses and non-deductible items (notional expenses, private expenses, bribes, penalties and 50% of entertainment, foreign tax paid without credit, depreciation in excess of capital allowances)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back expenses not incurred for the generation of taxable income in Cyprus; maintain contemporaneous records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: capital allowances (wear and tear, annual allowance on plant/machinery, industrial buildings), NID, IP regime deduction, group relief and donations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only capital allowances attributable to the Cypriot PE or fixed base
